name: Kettle River (Minnesota)

gaugeContext.note: USGS 05336700 is on the Kettle River below Sandstone, downstream of the Musclewood trip and upstream of the Highway 48–Maple Island trip. Tributaries and distance separate it from these reaches. It provides river-flow context; no local rapid threshold or travel-speed calibration is assigned.

timing.note: No reviewed flow-to-speed model or numeric trip-time range is assigned. DNR describes a full-day paddle; do not calculate hours from its general paddling-speed advice.

blurb: Two DNR-recommended Kettle River paddles: a full-day trip from Musclewood to Highway 23, and a shorter 7.2-mile trip from Highway 48 to Maple Island. Compare rapids, public access areas and park restrictions before choosing your stretch.

sections.notes: DNR recommends this full-day trip through wooded river country. Expect rapids, changing water levels and active paddling. Arrange a shuttle and locate the Highway 23 exit beforehand. This trip finishes above the more difficult Banning rapids.

distanceEvidence.note: Published approximate river miles: 46.3 minus 29.8 equals 16.5. The DNR trip page independently states 16.5 miles. GIS lists Musclewood as 46.2; retain the published trip distance rather than silently mixing source mileages. Parking carries and shuttle mileage are excluded.

notices.title: Rapids before the takeout
notices.text: DNR identifies Class I–II rapids between river miles 33.5 and 32. Levels respond to rain; check current river guidance and scout when needed. The gauge below Sandstone does not establish conditions at every rapid.
notices.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — Kettle River trip guidance

notices.title: Banning construction: use the Highway 23 exit
notices.text: DNR announced that most of Banning State Park, including its interior river access, closes November 9, 2026 for construction. Its notice lists Highway 23 as an available alternative. This trip ends there; do not continue to #2 expecting it to be open. Check current park alerts before leaving home.

sections.routeReview: Approximate DNR water-trail course. Exact landing connections are not drawn, and the line is not a recommended navigation channel.

putInAccess.operator: Minnesota DNR, Division of Parks and Trails
putInAccess.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — Kettle River map 1 and public water-access inventory
putInAccess.note: The published DNR coordinate is retained unchanged. Imagery places it in the wooded access approach; the precise water-edge landing is not resolved. The GIS name says Musclewood Lake, but its water-trail ID, directions and the DNR river map identify this Kettle River site. The GIS river mile is 46.2; the recommended trip and printed map use 46.3, which governs the published 16.5-mile trip.
putInAccess.directions: From Highway 61 south of Sturgeon Lake, follow County Road 52 west to the Kettle River bridge. Use the public carry-in area northwest of the bridge and inspect the path to the water. The marker identifies the access area under trees, not an exact shoreline landing. Arrange your vehicle shuttle before launching.

takeOutAccess.operator: Minnesota DNR, Division of Parks and Trails
takeOutAccess.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — Kettle River map 1 and public water-access inventory
takeOutAccess.note: The DNR GPS site coordinate is retained unchanged. It falls on the gravel turnaround/ramp area beside the river, rather than a resolved water-edge landing. Keep an approximate area marker and accept reviewed suggestions. DNR’s October 23, 2026 construction notice identifies Highway 23 as an available alternative to the closed access inside Banning State Park.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the public gravel access north of Highway 23, about 2.5 miles west of Askov. DNR places it on the left bank facing downstream, just before the highway bridge. Identify the exit during your shuttle and finish here; Banning State Park’s #2 access is a different site farther downstream.

sections.difficulty: Mostly flat water; Class I rapid
sections.notes: A DNR-recommended shorter paddle through forest, with a Class I rapid near river mile 11. Finish at Maple Island before the Lower Kettle rapids. Arrange the park-road shuttle before launching and allow for carrying boats at the takeout.

distanceEvidence.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — Kettle River map 2, recommended day trip
distanceEvidence.streamId: Kettle River State Water Trail, Minnesota
distanceEvidence.note: The DNR map and trip page publish 7.2 miles (15.1 minus 7.9). The GIS access inventory lists Maple Island at mile 8.0; do not mix that value with the published trip. Carries and vehicle shuttle are excluded.

notices.title: Finish before the Lower Kettle rapids
notices.text: DNR recommends exiting at Maple Island at river mile 7.9. The Class I–II Lower Kettle rapids begin around mile 7.8 downstream. This trip also includes a Class I rapid near mile 11; check water levels and scout as needed.

notices.title: Maple Island: plan for carrying your boat
notices.text: The park map and GIS list carry-in access; the water-trail map calls this a trailer access. Confirm current vehicle and ramp arrangements with the park before bringing a trailered boat. A park vehicle permit is required.
notices.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — St. Croix State Park map

notices.title: 2026 park closures and road work
notices.text: St. Croix State Park lists full public closures November 19–22 and December 1–6, 2026 for deer hunts. Do not plan a Maple Island takeout during those closures. Entrance-road paving continues into November with one lane open; check current park alerts before arranging your shuttle.
notices.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — St. Croix State Park alerts

sections.routeReview: Approximate DNR water-trail course. Exact landing connections are not drawn. Finish at Maple Island before the downstream rapids; the line is not a recommended navigation channel.

putInAccess.operator: Minnesota DNR, Division of Parks and Trails
putInAccess.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — Kettle River map 2, park map and public access inventory
putInAccess.note: DNR GPS facility coordinate retained unchanged. Satellite imagery shows a riverbank access clearing just south of the Highway 48 bridge; canopy obscures the precise landing. The inventory lists a concrete trailer launch but its north-of-road directions conflict with the coordinate. Keep an approximate area marker and seek a reviewed shoreline correction.
putInAccess.directions: Use the public access at the Highway 48 bridge over the Kettle River, about four miles east of Hinckley. DNR places it on river right facing downstream. Inspect the signed driveway during your shuttle: the inventory says north of the road, while its coordinate and imagery place the access area immediately south of the bridge. The area marker does not locate the exact ramp edge.

takeOutAccess.operator: Minnesota DNR, Division of Parks and Trails
takeOutAccess.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — Kettle River map 2, park map and public access inventory
takeOutAccess.note: DNR GPS facility coordinate retained unchanged; it marks a clearing back from the water. The 2026 water-trail map calls #6 a trailer access, while the current park map and GIS describe carry-in access. Do not promise trailer access. The trip guide uses river mile 7.9, while GIS says 8.0; use the published 7.2-mile recommended trip. Exact shoreline position remains unresolved.
takeOutAccess.directions: Reach Maple Island through St. Croix State Park using the park road map and posted signs. The park map shows a parking area and carry-in access on the left bank facing downstream. Identify the exit before launching and arrange your shuttle; do not continue into the Lower Kettle rapids to look for another landing. Check seasonal road and park closures.

mapAuditNote: Both DNR-recommended trips have reviewed approximate access areas. Exact landing positions and river-course geometry are separate reviews.
